Artificial Intelligence Accurately Detects Breast Arterial Calcification on Routine Mammograms

Artificial intelligence systems can accurately identify breast arterial calcifications on routine mammography, according to a systematic review evaluating diagnostic performance across multiple clinical datasets. The review analyzed findings from five studies encompassing 12,924 mammography cases, comparing automated detection algorithms directly against manual assessments performed by radiologists to evaluate whether machine learning tools could reliably pinpoint vascular markers.

Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide and disproportionately affects women. Although breast arterial calcifications have emerged as a sex-specific predictor of cardiovascular risk, routine clinical reporting has remained inconsistent because standard evaluation guidelines are currently lacking. Consequently, automated artificial intelligence models have attracted attention as an objective mechanism to identify these calcifications during regular mammography examinations.

To assess algorithmic precision, researchers conducted a systematic search across major databases, including MEDLINE, PubMed Central, Scopus, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, and ClinicalTrials.gov for literature published between 2015 and 2025. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, two independent reviewers screened 84 initial records and extracted data using Covidence, while applying the QUADAS-2 tool to evaluate potential study bias before synthesizing results.

The analyzed machine learning models demonstrated robust diagnostic capability when compared with radiologist-generated ground truth. Across the included investigations, artificial intelligence tools achieved Area Under the Curve values ranging from 0.84 to 0.96. System performance also yielded diagnostic sensitivities between 0.696 and 0.87, specificities between 0.92 and 0.98, overall accuracies between 0.81 and 0.998, precisions between 0.683 and 0.89, and F1-scores between 0.665 and 0.87.

Despite minor variability across evaluated platforms, the consistently high metrics indicate that automated systems can effectively augment manual interpretation workflows without displacing radiologist oversight. While the authors emphasize that larger and more diverse cohorts remain necessary to validate broader generalizability, current evidence demonstrates that artificial intelligence can reliably detect calcifications and help address an unmet need in preventive cardiovascular care for women.

Subject of Research: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence for detecting breast arterial calcification on mammography

Article Title: Artificial intelligence for breast arterial calcification detection on mammography: A systematic review of diagnostic accuracy

Article References: Campbell, A. P., Petfield, L., Nemec II, E. C., & Rose, S. J. (2026). Artificial intelligence for breast arterial calcification detection on mammography: A systematic review of diagnostic accuracy. PLOS Digital Health, 5(11), e0001829. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pdig.0001829
